texts.preamble: In Re:- Radhanath Mondal vs Re: An Application For Bail Under ... on 15 March, 2016 Author: Ashim Kumar Roy Bench: Ashim Kumar Roy 1 32 15.3.2016 pd. C.R.M. No. 2058 of 2016 In re:- Radhanath Mondal ... Petitioner. -And- Re: An application for bail under Section 439 Cr.P.C. affirmed on 9.3.2016 in connection with Moyna Police Station Case No.228/2015 dated 28.9.2015 under Sections 272/273 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 read with West Bengal Act 42 of 1973 and Sections 3/304/120B of the Indian Penal Code. 1860 and Section 46Aa of the Bengal Excise Act 1909 and Section 16(3) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act 1954.
texts.facts: The petitioner is in custody for six months. According to the case of the prosecution, total 28 persons died by consuming spurious and poisonous country liquor. However, it is an admitted position that only in respect of ten persons, post mortem was held and so far as the balance eighteen persons are concerned, they were cremated without any post mortem . The F.S.L. Report of the victim also supports the prosecution case. Now, the prayer for bail of the petitioner has been opposed from the side of the State by referring the statements of the witnesses, which are at pages 19 and 20 of the Case Diary. In Re:- Radhanath Mondal vs Re: An Application For Bail Under ... on 15 March, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111845511/ 1 It appears that although according to the aforesaid witnesses, one Dulal Bisui and Manik Ruidas are the principal accused and from their possession, huge quantity of poisonous I.D. Liquor was seized but from the possession of the present petitioner, only a two litres bottle containing one litre of such I.D. Liquor was recovered and on examination of the same, it was found to have contain poisonous element.
texts.arguments: The learned Counsel for the petitioner, in his usual fairness, contends that the petitioner was possessing the said I.D.Liquor for his own consumption.
texts.petitioner_arguments: The learned Counsel for the petitioner, in his usual fairness, contends that the petitioner was possessing the said I.D.Liquor for his own consumption.
